title: Target evaluation of a quasicategorical lax comma construction
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets, spaces and degreewise simplicial pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], composition of mapping spaces of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and inner and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. All objects fit in one fixed universe. Let $f:A\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories that lifts equivalence edges with specified source. Form
$$T=A\times_{f,B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B),\qquad q=\operatorname{ev}_1:T\to B.$$
Then $T$ is a quasicategory and $q$ is a cocartesian fibration. Its objects are $(a,u:f(a)\to b)$. For $x=(a,u:f(a)\to b)$ and $y=(a',v:f(a')\to b')$ there is a natural equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_T(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_A(a,a')\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_B(f(a),b')}\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b').$$
The two maps to the middle space are $h\mapsto v f(h)$ and $k\mapsto k u$, respectively. The homotopy pullback retains the path between these composites. Under this equivalence $q$ is projection to $k$, and precomposition and postcomposition agree with pasting coherent squares. Here $X\times_Z^hY$ denotes the path-space pullback of spaces, with its paths and all higher simplices. These assertions remain valid when $A$ is empty; no limits, colimits or presentability of $A$ or $B$ are assumed.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.7.12, printed p. 143 (PDF p. 161), dualized, for the cocartesian projection; Corollary 2.4.7.11 for endpoint evaluation. Mapping formula: oriented fiber product of Kerodon Subsection 4.6.4 (Kerodon 01KE), Definition 4.6.4.1 and Proposition 4.6.4.2, together with the coherent-square description of morphisms. WANTED archived HTT and Kerodon. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$ and let $e=(\operatorname{ev}_0,\operatorname{ev}_1):E\to B\times B$. The exponential isofibration theorem applied to $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ makes $e$ an isofibration between quasicategories. The map $(f,\operatorname{id}_B):A\times B\to B\times B$ therefore has degreewise pullback $T$, so the isofibration pullback theorem makes $T$ a quasicategory. The projection $A\times B\to B$ is an inner fibration by the horn definition (fill the $A$-coordinate while the $B$-coordinate is the prescribed simplex), and the pullback projection $T\to A\times B$ is an inner fibration; hence their composite $q=\operatorname{ev}_1:T\to B$ is an inner fibration.

source.place: Exponentiation for endpoint evaluation; the pullback/quasicategory conclusion is the cited isofibration pullback theorem.

proof.text: Fix $x=(a,u:f(a)\to b)$ and $y=(a',v:f(a')\to b')$ in $T$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback] with $\mathcal C=A$, $F=f$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal B=B$ and $G=\operatorname{id}_B$; it allows arbitrary functors. Its pullback is $E'=A\times_{f,B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B,\operatorname{id}}B$. The degreewise map $T\to E'$, $(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto(\alpha,\operatorname{ev}_1\beta,\beta)$, is an isomorphism of simplicial sets, since the last coordinate of a simplex of $E'$ is forced to be $\operatorname{ev}_1\beta$. It carries $q$ to the target projection $p$, and $x,y$ to $(a,b,u)$, $(a',b',v)$. Transport along this isomorphism gives a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_T(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_A(a,a')\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_B(f(a),b')}\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b')$, with legs $h\mapsto vf(h)$ and $k\mapsto\operatorname{id}_B(k)u=ku$, retaining the path and all higher simplices. Under it $q$ is the actual projection to $k$, and composition is pasting of coherent squares. Explicitly, for an edge $(h_0,k_0,\gamma_0):x_0\to x$, precomposition sends $(h,k,\gamma)$ to $(hh_0,kk_0)$ with path $\gamma f(h_0)$ followed by $k\gamma_0$. For $(h_1,k_1,\gamma_1):y\to y_1$, postcomposition gives $(h_1h,k_1k)$ with path $\gamma_1f(h)$ followed by $k_1\gamma$. The composition and unit homotopies are those of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. This proves the displayed mapping formula and the composition assertions.

source.place: Hom-functor pullback square for oriented fiber products, specialized to G = id_B through the existing general comma mapping-space node.

proof.text: Let $x=(a,u:f(a)\to b)$ and let $k:b\to b'$ be an edge of $B$. Fill the inner $2$-horn with consecutive edges $u,k$ in the quasicategory $B$; call its third edge $w:f(a)\to b'$ and its $2$-simplex $\sigma$. Triangulate $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ by its diagonal from $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$, with the first coordinate the transformation direction and the second the arrow direction. Send its four vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)$ to $f(a),f(a),b,b'$. On the triangle $((0,0),(0,1),(1,1))$ use $\sigma$, and on $((0,0),(1,0),(1,1))$ use the degenerate triangle with edges $1_{f(a)},w,w$. They agree on the diagonal, so define an edge $u\to w$ in $E$, with source endpoint the constant edge at $f(a)$ and target endpoint exactly $k$. Together with the constant edge at $a$ this is an edge $s:x\to y=(a,w)$ of the degreewise pullback $T$, and $q(s)=k$. The construction also covers degenerate $k$.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.7.12, opposite-category dual; agent expansion by the explicit two-triangle square.

proof.text:
Fix $z=(a',v:f(a')\to c)$. Put $H=\operatorname{Map}_A(a,a')$, $Z=\operatorname{Map}_B(f(a),c)$, $L'=\operatorname{Map}_B(b',c)$, and $L=\operatorname{Map}_B(b,c)$. Step 2 identifies $\operatorname{Map}_T(y,z)$ with $H\times_Z^h L'$ using precomposition by $w$, and $\operatorname{Map}_T(x,z)$ with $H\times_Z^h L$ using precomposition by $u$. In both cases $H\to Z$ is $h\mapsto vf(h)$. The triangle $\sigma$ of Step 3 gives the specified commutation homotopy between precomposition by $w$ and the composite of precomposition by $k:L'\to L$ with precomposition by $u:L\to Z$. The two defining homotopy-pullback squares to $H\to Z$ therefore form an adjacent diagram
$(H\times_Z^h L'\longrightarrow H\times_Z^h L\longrightarrow H)$ over $(L'\xrightarrow{k^*}L\longrightarrow Z)$, with vertical maps the second projections and $H\to Z$.
The right square and the outer rectangle are homotopy pullbacks by their path-space definitions. Homotopy-pullback pasting (with the homotopy supplied by $\sigma$) proves that the left square is a homotopy pullback. On triples its top map sends $(h,\ell,\gamma)$ to $(h,\ell k,\gamma')$, where $\gamma'$ pastes $\gamma$ with the triangle comparing $\ell w$ and $(\ell k)u$. This is precomposition with the actual edge $s$ by the pasting description of composition in Step 2; its $A$-component is precomposition with the degenerate identity and hence the identity up to its specified unit homotopy. Thus the left square is exactly the mapping-space square for $s$ over $k$, including its specified commutation homotopy, not merely a square of homotopy classes. Applying the cocartesian mapping criterion to the inner fibration $q$ of Step 1 proves that $s$ is $q$-cocartesian.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.1.11 (specified-homotopy pasting), followed by the cited dual of HTT Proposition 2.4.4.3.

proof.text: Step 1 gives that $q$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories, and Steps 3 and 4 supply a $q$-cocartesian lift of every edge $k:q(x)\to b'$ with prescribed source $x$. By the definition of cocartesian fibration, $q$ is therefore a cocartesian fibration. The mapping formula of Step 2 and the coherent pasting description remain valid when $A$ is empty (there are then no vertices to test and all lifting assertions are vacuous); the pullback construction uses no limits, colimits, presentability, or nonemptiness assumptions.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.7.12, opposite-category dual; conclusion from the definition and the preceding construction.
